title: Constant geometric degree makes a separated etale chart finite
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], $W$ a scheme, and $f:W\to X$ a representable etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Suppose $f$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests (inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact) and separated (its representable diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]). Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose for every map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point], the geometric fibre $W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] has exactly $d$ points. Then $f$ is finite locally free of degree $d$ on every scheme test [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and remains etale. Neither $X$ nor $W$ is assumed Noetherian or of finite type over $S$.

source.place: Tag 07S8, lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification, universal property on the degree-d stratum; etale case, using geometric cardinality as degree.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary scheme test $a:T\to X$ and put $Y=W\times_XT$, $p:Y\to T$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], representability makes $Y$ a scheme and representable etaleness makes $p$ etale. The quasi-compactness assumption on scheme tests makes $p$ quasi-compact. Its diagonal is the scheme test of $\Delta_f$ along $Y\times_TY\to W\times_XW$ (both represent pairs of sections with equal image); $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion by the separatedness hypothesis, so its base change $\Delta_p$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], and $p$ is separated. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $p$ is flat, locally of finite presentation and unramified. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points] to obtain that $p$ is locally quasi-finite. No property of the structure maps to $S$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 07S8 (lemma-quasi-compact-reasonable-stratification), reduction to scheme tests; morphisms.tex Tag 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite).

proof.text: For $t\in T$, let $k=\kappa(t)$ and $F=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}k$. The base change of the quasi-compact scheme morphism $p$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change]; hence $F$ is quasi-compact, since $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], $F$ is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions $L_i/k$. Its singleton components are open, so quasi-compactness gives finitely many of them. Each $\operatorname{Spec}L_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]: a field basis finitely generates $L_i$ as a $k$-module. Induction with [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct] makes their finite disjoint union finite over $k$; the empty case is $\operatorname{Spec}0$, finite because its section algebra is the zero module. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim], write $F=\operatorname{Spec}B$ for its finite-dimensional section algebra, and set $e_t=\dim_k B$.

Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $k$ and the geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change] applied to $p$ and $\bar t$, the fibre $E=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is finite of degree $e_t$ over $\Omega$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $E$ with $W\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for $a\bar t$: both give a section of $W$ and a section of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with the same image in $X$. Thus $E$ has exactly $d$ points by the hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] to the etale projection $E\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, which is etale by representability of $f$. Every component is the spectrum of a finite separable extension of $\Omega$; that extension equals $\Omega$, since the minimal polynomial of any element is irreducible and splits over $\Omega$, hence has degree one. Consequently $E$ is a disjoint union of exactly $d$ copies of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The sheaf condition on this disjoint open cover identifies its section algebra with $\Omega^d$, whose coordinate vectors are a basis of size $d$. It follows that $e_t=d$, including $d=0$ when the section algebra is zero.

All fibres of $p$ are finite of degree $d$ by steps 2--3, so $d$ is a universal fibre-degree bound. Together with step 1 this supplies every hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-lqf-bounded-stratification]. Apply it to $p$ and obtain its strata $T_r$. For each $t\in T$, the pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is finite by step 2, flat and locally of finite presentation because it is etale by representability of $f$, and has degree $d$ by step 3. By [def-pc-finite-locally-free] it is therefore finite locally free of degree $d$. The universal property in the cited stratification theorem, applied to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$, gives $t\in T_d$. Hence $|T|=T_d$. Apply the same universal property to $\mathrm{id}_T$ to conclude that $p$ itself is finite locally free of degree $d$. It is etale already by step 1. Since $T\to X$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion on every scheme test. If $T$ is empty the containment in $T_d$ is vacuous and the same universal property applies; no nonemptiness, Noetherianity or finite-type assumption has entered.
